vectors.desc: UINT-16 65535 into a java Short target: range-check reject, never wraparound
deriv: UINT-16 max: DESC E0 D8 0B 02, value body direct (no zigzag) 65535 on the u16 rung — 39 FF FF (WF-9 :363-366; WF-7 :288-289)

java Short is signed 16-bit: 65535 sits outside — the declared policy is a decode-side range check with blame (overflow_value), values outside reject loudly, never silent wraparound (java.md 2.1 :217); char is the only unsigned integral type and its range rule is 0..FFFF as a UTF-16 code unit (java.md 2.1 :201-207) (WF-9)
rust u16 and go uint16 are native — the same bytes materialize; the degradation is a property of the consuming projection, encoded per-vector in the consumers map

vectors.desc: UINT-16 32767 into a java Short target: in-range materialization, the range-check pass
deriv: 32767 = Short.MAX_VALUE: the boundary companion of V-120 — one count below, the value sits inside the target's representable range and materializes (u16 rung 39 7F FF, WF-7 :288-289)

the java row is a range-check gate, not a width gate: values within the target's representable range materialize in the next wider signed type, values outside reject loudly (java.md 2.1 :217) — this leg documents the pass side of that check in the consumers map (WF-9)
all-ok consumers: the vector carries the family's boundary; the reject side rides V-120 (D3 unsigned_range)

vectors.desc: non-UTF-8 STRING: rust String/java String targets reject, go string carries
deriv: envelope (c4 DD r5): root DESC E0 D8 0D — STRING kind 13, empty body (WF-22 :624)
STRING length 2, raw bytes 61 FF: any byte sequence is legal — there is no UTF-8 validity gate in the core; a string is a byte sequence, not mandated text (WF-13 :419-421)

rust String/str are always valid UTF-8 (std:str): decode-side an invalid sequence into a String or str target rejects — invalid_string_encoding (rust.md 2.1 :202); java String is UTF-16-sourced, invalid UTF-8 has no String image — invalid_string_encoding (java.md 2.1 :218); the gate is loud in both directions, never a lossy default (WF-13)
go strings are byte sequences — the value carries natively (go.md 5.2 strings row :611); the escape hatch for rust/java is Vec<u8>/byte[] as BLOB (V-123) (WF-14)

vectors.desc: BLOB escape hatch: byte[]/Vec<u8> carry the bytes no String target admits

Vec<u8> carries all bytes (rust.md 2.1 :202), byte[] carries all bytes (java.md 2.1 :218), []byte is the native BLOB (go.md 1.4 :171-172) — the STRING/BLOB class split is the wire image of the projections' text-versus-binary distinction (WF-13; WF-14)
